title: Favorite tunes and keys
summary: Tunes he likes to play, his range limits now, and his preference for the blues in E flat then F.

blocks.x: I was going to ask you about different tunes that you like in particular.

Well it all depends on how you feel, Dick. When your lip is right you like the ones you're going to show off and not make any clinkers. But there's a lot of good tunes, Dick. Now Chris and I, we practice a lot together and Chris likes Wolverine blues. And Chris likes Big Bud and Eggman the way we play it. And he knocks hell out of the Hindu stand. But that's a crip. That's as easy as the Saints. And I used to really like Deed I Do. It's a Tin Pan Alley tune, but I always did like it. Sleepy down the South I always liked. Of course the range is a little high for me now. I used to take it up to around the high C anyway. I'd stick between the G's and occasionally an F. I mean an A. But I don't go too high anymore. But that was that tune we were trying to record up at Tulane. It came out so scratchy and we'd give it to you good before you leave. But those are wonderful. Someday you'll be sorry. And of course the blues. Everybody loves the blues. And I like it slow in E flat and I like to pick it up in the key of F. Now that's one of my idiosyncrasies. It's not an idiosyncrasies, but it's something that's stupid but makes me feel better if I do it. Which is the definition of an idiosyncrasies.
